top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) is the mature, independently confirmed case: 1e-18 class performance has been reproduced at JILA/NIST, RIKEN/Tokyo, SYRTE and PTB, the magic-wavelength idea is a single clean physical criterion, the pair has the cleanest attribution on the slate, and the clocks already yield physical results (millimetre-scale redshift, limits on constants and dark-matter couplings). The citation should name the lattice clock and not the redefinition of the second. I rank P002 second because the flat-band prediction and the correlated phases are robust across many groups, though the field is young and credit is crowded; P003 third because the diffuse neutrino flux is secure but individual sources remain at 3-4 sigma and the Halzen/Spiering allocation needs expert review. A prize now is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; P003 (IceCube) is in my broad astroparticle field but I have no listed collaboration or institutional tie to Halzen or Spiering
